title: The PearlAI Framework: Leveraging Artificial Intelligence to Transform Education in Africa
venue: International Journal of Scientific Research in Computer Science, Engineering and Information Technology
extended_summary:
This paper addresses the persistent challenges facing education systems in Africa, including limited access, inequity, low learning outcomes, weak teacher support, and curriculum relevance. Rather than reporting a single empirical intervention, it proposes the PearlAI Framework as an Africa-centered, open-source approach for using artificial intelligence to improve education at scale.

The framework is built around six domains: access and equity, teacher workforce support, literacy and numeracy, curriculum relevance, assessment and evaluation, and student engagement and motivation. It draws on a systematic review of literature following PRISMA guidelines, synthesizing evidence from African and global research on mother-tongue instruction, formative assessment, retrieval practice, culturally responsive pedagogy, AI feedback systems, and teacher co-pilots. The review searched major databases, screened studies, and included 34 papers in the final synthesis.

The paper argues that effective AI in education must augment teachers rather than replace them, and that context-sensitive design is essential for African settings. It highlights the importance of offline-first deployment, small language models, privacy protections, modular architecture, and sustained teacher professional development. The main conclusion is that AI can improve learning and system efficiency only when integrated with pedagogy, local language and culture, and strong implementation and governance structures.

identified_tools.name: GenAI (General)
identified_tools.description: A generic generative AI / large language model chatbot or AI assistant used for educational support such as feedback, tutoring, lesson planning, and content adaptation.
identified_tools.use_case: The paper proposes PearlAI as an AI framework that includes generative AI-enabled teacher coaching, automated lesson planning, adaptive tutoring, and AI-driven formative feedback, but it does not evaluate a specific named commercial product.

quality_tier_rationale: This is a conceptual and synthesis paper proposing the PearlAI framework and summarizing prior literature; it does not report original empirical evaluation of a specific AI tool in this paper. The methodology is a PRISMA-guided review, but the paper itself provides no primary outcome data for the proposed system.
impact_tier_rationale: Because the paper is a framework proposal rather than an intervention study, there is no direct measured impact attributable to PearlAI in this article. The proposed design targets potentially meaningful effects on teacher workload and instructional quality, but these remain untested here.
